title: R. P. Feynman on the difference between knowing the name of something and knowing something.
summary: A two-minute clip of Richard Feynman on the difference between knowing the name of something and actually knowing it. He uses the example of knowing a bird's name in every language and still knowing nothing about the bird.
why: It is the standard reference whenever a thread turns to rote labels versus real understanding.

quote.text: Feynman also knows the difference "between knowing the name of something and knowing something"
